name: KnowWhereGraph
team: UCSB and collaborators; Janowicz, Hitzler, Schildhauer, Zhu et al.
summary: Connects environmental and societal datasets through shared spatial references for interdisciplinary discovery and geo-enrichment.
paper: The KnowWhereGraph: A Large-Scale Geo-Knowledge Graph for Interdisciplinary Knowledge Discovery and Geo-Enrichment (2026)

name: DDE Geoscience Knowledge Graph
team: IUGS Deep-time Digital Earth programme
summary: Organises geoscience concepts and disciplinary knowledge within the Deep-time Digital Earth programme.
paper: DDE geoscience knowledge systems and graph research

name: The World Avatar
team: University of Cambridge, CARES and collaborators; Markus Kraft et al.
summary: A dynamic knowledge graph and software-agent ecosystem linking physical assets, observations and computational models in digital twins.
paper: The World Avatar: A world model for facilitating interoperability (2021)

name: Geoconnex
team: Internet of Water Coalition, USGS and partners
summary: Connects hydrologic features with distributed water data using persistent identifiers and linked-data knowledge graphs.
paper: Geoconnex knowledge graph access documentation

name: Ocean Data Information System
team: UNESCO-IOC International Oceanographic Data and Information Exchange
summary: Federates ocean information systems through interoperable metadata and a shared discovery knowledge graph.
paper: ODIS architecture and implementation

name: Km4City / Snap4City
team: DISIT Lab, University of Florence; Paolo Nesi and collaborators
summary: An RDF city knowledge model and smart-city platform connecting transport, services, sensors and urban resources.
paper: Km4City urban knowledge model

name: YAGO2geo
team: University of Athens; Nikos Karalis, Georgios Mandilaras, Manolis Koubarakis
summary: Extends YAGO2 with detailed geographic geometries and spatial relations for geometry-aware queries.
paper: Extending the YAGO2 knowledge graph with precise geospatial knowledge (2019)

name: WorldKG
team: Dsouza, Tempelmeier, Yu, Gottschalk and Demidova
summary: Builds a geographic knowledge graph from OpenStreetMap, with an ontology that makes heterogeneous tags and entity types easier to query.
paper: WorldKG: A World-Scale Geographic Knowledge Graph (2021)

name: YAGO2
team: Max Planck Institute for Informatics; Hoffart, Suchanek, Berberich and Weikum
summary: A general knowledge graph with explicit temporal and spatial information; provides the foundation extended by YAGO2geo.
paper: YAGO2: A Spatially and Temporally Enhanced Knowledge Base from Wikipedia (2013)

name: LinkedGeoData
team: Leipzig AKSW; Stadler, Lehmann, Höffner and Auer
summary: Publishes OpenStreetMap features as RDF linked data and connects spatial entities to external knowledge bases.
paper: LinkedGeoData: A Core for a Web of Spatial Open Data (2012)

name: Wikidata geographic knowledge
team: Wikimedia community; Denny Vrandečić and Markus Krötzsch
summary: The geographic part of a general-purpose collaborative knowledge graph, including places, coordinates and administrative relationships.
paper: Wikidata: A Free Collaborative Knowledgebase (2014)

name: DBpedia geographic knowledge
team: DBpedia community; Lehmann, Auer, Bizer and collaborators
summary: The geographic part of a multilingual general knowledge graph extracted from Wikipedia, supporting place linking and cross-domain queries.
paper: DBpedia: A Large-Scale, Multilingual Knowledge Base Extracted from Wikipedia (2015)

name: GeoNames Linked Data
team: GeoNames project
summary: Provides geographic names, feature types and administrative relationships through stable entity identifiers and RDF representations.
paper: GeoNames Ontology and Semantic Web documentation

name: Tourism-KG for interpretable recommendation
team: Jialiang Gao, Peng Peng, Feng Lu, Christophe Claramunt and Yang Xu
summary: Uses tourism knowledge graphs to represent destination attributes and disentangle tourist decision-making for interpretable travel recommendations.
paper: Towards travel recommendation interpretability: Disentangling tourist decision-making process via knowledge graph (2023)

name: Tourism spatial competitive intelligence
team: Jialiang Gao, Peng Peng, Feng Lu, Shu Wang, Xiaogang Xie and Christophe Claramunt
summary: Applies tourism knowledge graphs to analyse relationships between destination characteristics and spatial competition.
paper: Knowledge-driven spatial competitive intelligence for tourism (2024)

name: UUKG
team: HKUST (Guangzhou), HKUST and Alibaba Cloud; Yansong Ning, Hao Liu, Hao Wang, Zhenyu Zeng and Hui Xiong
summary: Public urban knowledge graphs for New York and Chicago, linking urban entities and supporting taxi, bike, crowd, crime and service-demand prediction.
paper: UUKG: Unified Urban Knowledge Graph Dataset for Urban Spatiotemporal Prediction (2023)

name: Maritime element knowledge graph
team: Y. Li, X. Liu, Z. Wang, Q. Mei, W. Xie, Y. Yang and P. Wang
summary: Builds a maritime semantic schema and knowledge graph connecting vessels, navigation infrastructure and activity information for automated decision-making.
paper: Construction of a large-scale maritime element semantic schema based on knowledge graph models for unmanned automated decision-making (2024)

name: Ship-collision accident knowledge graph
team: Langxiong Gan, Beiyan Ye, Zhiqiu Huang, Yi Xu, Qiaohong Chen and Yaqing Shu
summary: Extracts structured accident knowledge from ship-collision reports and supports case retrieval for maritime safety investigation.
paper: Knowledge graph construction based on ship collision accident reports to improve maritime traffic safety (2023)

name: SceneKG
team: Y. Huang, Y. He, Y. Sheng and collaborators
summary: Represents geographic scenes as contextualised spatiotemporal knowledge, incorporating geographic processes and their interactions.
paper: SceneKG: A Geo-Scene Based Spatiotemporal Knowledge Representation Framework Considering Geo-Processes

name: Cascading-disaster causal knowledge graph
team: Yuanyuan Tian and Wenwen Li
summary: Extracts causal links between disaster events using semantic rules, spatiotemporal co-occurrence and event descriptions.
paper: GeoAI for Knowledge Graph Construction: Identifying Causality Between Cascading Events to Support Environmental Resilience Research (2022)

name: Landslide susceptibility knowledge graph
team: Xuexi Yang, Qian Xu, Qinghao Liu, Xin Hu and collaborators
summary: Combines domain knowledge extraction, graph construction and rule mining to support interpretable landslide susceptibility evaluation.
paper: Towards Intelligent Landslide Susceptibility Evaluation: Knowledge Extraction and Rule Mining (2025)

name: Disaster-chain observation event logic graph
team: Yunbo Zhang, Wenjie Chen, Bingshu Huang and collaborators
summary: Uses an observation-event logic ontology and instantiated graph knowledge to plan geographic observations across disaster-chain stages.
paper: An event logic graph for geographic environment observation planning in disaster chain monitoring (2024)

name: EcoLink
team: Tim Alamenciak, C. A. Arnillas, H. Caufield and collaborators
summary: Develops a LinkML-based knowledge graph schema for environmental variables, ecological processes and their relationships in complex environmental systems.
paper: EcoLink: Towards a Knowledge Graph Schema for Complex Environmental Systems (2025)

name: GLEAN dynamic event knowledge graphs
team: Songgaojun Deng, Huzefa Rangwala and Yue Ning
summary: Constructs dynamic event-actor graphs and combines relational and textual contexts to forecast multiple event types and participants.
paper: Dynamic Knowledge Graph Based Multi-Event Forecasting (2020)

name: LLM4Geopolitics
team: Amira Mouakher, Nuno Morgado and Farah Ftouhi
summary: Combines event knowledge graph representations and large language models for contextual geopolitical event forecasting.
paper: LLM4Geopolitics: A Framework Leveraging Large Language Models for Predicting Geopolitical Events (2026)

name: Formal geographic knowledge graph model
team: Shu Wang, Xueying Zhang, Peng Ye, Mi Du, Yanxu Lu and Haonan Xue
summary: Formalises geographic knowledge representation through geographic objects, concepts and relationships, including states and changes.
paper: Geographic Knowledge Graph (GeoKG): A Formalized Geographic Knowledge Representation (2019)

name: Geographic evolutionary knowledge graph
team: Kun Zheng, Ming Hui Xie, Jin Biao Zhang, Juan Xie and Shu Hao Xia
summary: Models geographic entities, events and evolution to represent changing geographic processes and support spatiotemporal reasoning.
paper: A knowledge representation model based on the geographic spatiotemporal process (2022)

name: EventKG
team: L3S Research Center; Simon Gottschalk and Elena Demidova
summary: A multilingual event-centric temporal knowledge graph connecting events with entities, time and locations.
paper: EventKG: A Multilingual Event-Centric Temporal Knowledge Graph (2018)

name: GeoLink
team: EarthCube GeoLink consortium; geoscience repositories and semantic-web researchers
summary: Connects geoscience datasets, expeditions, samples, publications, researchers and funding through an RDF knowledge graph.
paper: The GeoLink Knowledge Graph (2018)

name: Geospatial data retrieval knowledge graph
team: Hao Li, Peng Yue, Haoru Wu, Baoxin Teng, Yongkun Zhao and Changfeng Liu
summary: Connects geospatial dataset knowledge with large language models to interpret natural-language questions and retrieve relevant geographic data.
paper: A Question-Answering Framework for Geospatial Data Retrieval Enhanced by a Knowledge Graph and Large Language Models (2025)
